les: Hoog en laag in dieselfde familie
kaps_punt: Onderwerp 4 - Waardeer en nadenke, Kwartaal 3. Die uitdrukkingskwaliteite van slaginstrumente in ŉ Afrika-musiekstuk. Klassifiseer verskeie instrumente as deel van ŉ familie of groep in terme van voorkoms, benoeming, hoe die klank voortgebring word en die toonhoogte klassifikasie (hoog-laag). Eie en ander se optredes en prosesse deur die gebruik van eenvoudige skeppende kunsterminologie.

items.bron: Loudness set by how hard the object is struck/plucked, pitch by the vibrating object's size/length: classroom sound-pitch activities (Biophysical Society lesson plan https://biophysics.org/Portals/0/BPSAssets/Education/Documents/BPS_LessonPlan_SoundPitch_Mar2025_sm.pdf ; GVSU sound activity https://www.gvsu.edu/cms4/asset/AF5F8044-C1CA-D385-2E8007C14930B056/sound_activity_description(3).pdf): 'the force of the plucking action determines the loudness'.

items.bron: Univ. of Rochester PHY103 'Drums' (drum sound modelled as a vibrating circular membrane), https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~sybenzvi/courses/phy103/2016f/phy103_drums.pdf ; Hornbostel-Sachs membranophone category (sound from a stretched membrane).

items.bron: Rochester PHY103 'Drums': fundamental of a circular membrane f = 0.766 x sqrt(T/sigma) / D, i.e. falls as diameter grows at the same tension. The 'gewoonlik' hedge is correct, since tension also sets pitch. https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~sybenzvi/courses/phy103/2016f/phy103_drums.pdf

items.bewering: Maar grootte is nie die hele antwoord nie. Die maker kan dieselfde vel stywer of slapper trek. 'n Stywer vel klink hoër, en 'n slapper vel klink laer.

items.bron: Same Rochester formula (frequency rises with tension T); Kettledrum patent EP0167280A1: 'the tension of the membrane is proportionally related to the frequency'. https://patents.google.com/patent/EP0167280A1/en

items.bewering: Baie Suid-Afrikaanse skole het 'n marimba met houtlatte in 'n ry.
items.bron: Education Africa International Marimba and Steelpan Festival expected close on 90 schools and institutions (africa.com, https://africa.com/headlines/the-8th-annual-education-africa-international-marimba-and-steelpan-festival-is-here); school programmes reported at Aqua Vista Primary (Daily Dispatch, 2017), Goede Hoop (Boksburg), Brebner Primary, Inkwenkwezi Secondary; Cape Town Marimba Festival since 2009. No national count exists, but 'baie' is supported.

items.bewering: Die lang latte klink laag, en die kort latte klink hoog.
items.bron: LibreTexts Physics 'Basic Acoustics of the Marimba': bar pitch depends on length, thickness and density; makers shorten a bar to raise its pitch. https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Waves_and_Acoustics/Acoustics/05%3A_Musical_Acoustics_Applications/5.02%3A_Basic_Acoustics_of_the_Marimba

items.bewering: 'n Liniaal wat oor 'n tafelrand uitsteek, wys ook dat 'n korter stuk hoër klink.
items.bron: Classroom ruler experiments: 'the shorter the ruler, the higher the sound' (SERC Carleton 'Exploring Sound: Length Makes a Difference', https://serc.carleton.edu/sp/mnstep/activities/19773.html ; TeachEngineering worksheet). Mapping checked: a ruler clamped at one end and a marimba bar resting on supports vibrate differently, but the direction carried over (shorter vibrating length -> higher pitch) holds for both. Comparing one ruler with itself, as the sentence does, avoids the stiffness caveat that applies when comparing different objects.

items.bewering: Die Chopi van suidelike Mosambiek speel hulle xilofone, wat hulle timbila noem.
items.bron: UNESCO ICH 'Chopi Timbila' (Masterpiece 2005, Representative List 2008): 'The Chopi communities live mainly in the southern part of Inhambane province in southern Mozambique'; orchestras of 'wooden xylophones, called timbila'. https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/chopi-timbila-00133 ; Wikipedia 'Timbila': mbila, plural timbila.

items.bewering: Die Chopi speel hulle timbila in 'n orkes. Daardie instrumente is met opset in verskillende groottes gebou.
items.blok: Een groep van klein tot groot
items.bron: UNESCO ICH 'Chopi Timbila': each orchestra uses 'five to thirty wooden xylophones, called timbila, of varying sizes and ranges of pitch'. https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/chopi-timbila-00133

items.bewering: Die klein chilanzane speel die hoogste klanke en die groot gulu die laagste.
items.blok: Een groep van klein tot groot
items.bron: ILAM (Rhodes University) Hugh Tracey recording 1963, Banguza, Mozambique: '2 Chilanzane (Treble), 8 Sange (Alto), 2 Doli (Tenor), 2 Debiinda (Bass), 2 Gulu (Double bass)'. https://digitalarchives.ru.ac.za/s/ilam/item/74079 . Wikipedia 'Timbila' also gives the gulu as the bass instrument, large enough to be played standing. Superlatives hold.

items.bewering: Tussen hulle in sit die sange, die doli en die debiinda.
items.blok: Een groep van klein tot groot
items.bron: ILAM Hugh Tracey 1963 listing (as above): Sange alto, Doli tenor, Debiinda bass, all between Chilanzane (treble) and Gulu (double bass). Spellings match ILAM's; other sources write sanje, dole, dibhinda/dibinda. https://digitalarchives.ru.ac.za/s/ilam/item/74079

items.bewering: Saam is hulle 'n groep binne die familie van slaginstrumente, en saam dek hulle die reeks van hoog tot laag.
items.blok: Een groep van klein tot groot
items.bron: Xylophones are percussion instruments (wooden bars struck with mallets; Wikipedia 'Xylophone'); the ensemble spans treble to double bass (ILAM listing above).

items.bewering: Die ngoma, met sy beesvel oor 'n wye opening gespan, hoort aan die lae kant.
items.bron: ERA/Royal Anthropological Institute, Venda Girls' Initiation, 'Venda Music' (after Kirby 1934): ngoma is 'a large, pot-shaped drum with hemispherical resonator carved out of solid wood'; the author labels ngoma, thungwa and murumba as bass, tenor and alto. https://era.anthropology.ac.uk/Era_Resources/Era/VendaGirls/VendaMusic/Mu_I_Text2.html ; museum record: 'the mouth is covered by an ox-hide that is stretched between pegs around the circumference of the rim', c. 80 cm across. https://wmic.net/venda-ngoma-drum/

items.bewering: Die hosho se klein sade ritsel skerp binne die kalbas.
items.bron: Grinnell College Musical Instrument Collection, 'Bira instruments from Zimbabwe' (hosho: dried gourd holding several dozen small hota seeds, Canna indica). https://omeka-s.grinnell.edu/s/MusicalInstruments/page/bira ; Wikipedia 'Hosho (instrument)'.

items.bewering: Die sand of klippies in ratels van gedroogde kokonne (kokonratels) rammel wanneer die danser beweeg.
items.bron: Brighton Museums: leg rattles of dried cocoons 'filled with small stones', worn around the legs when dancing (https://brightonmuseums.org.uk/?p=4986). Collector record of Zulu cocoon ankle rattles: cocoons 'filled with sand or small stones', sounding as dancers move (https://wmic.net/zulu-cocoon-ankle-rattles/). Pitt Rivers Museum: tied round dancers' lower legs. Note: 'klippies' is well attested; 'sand' rests on one collector record (Penn Museum lists the contents as 'seeds(?) or gravel(?)'), and the 'of' keeps the sentence true.

items.bewering: Die geskraapte bottel klink grof as jy oor sy riwwe skraap.
items.bron: OnMusic dictionary 'scraper': idiophones sounded by rubbing a stick over a ridged body; scraped vessels such as the güiro have a hollow body under the ridges (https://dev-dictionary.onmusic.org/terms/3040-scraper ; Horniman Museum H-S class 112.23 'scraped vessels'). A ridged bottle scraped this way is a scraped vessel, and its sound is a rasp. 'Grof' is a description, not a measurable claim.

items.bewering: Nie een van die laaste drie het 'n vaste plek tussen hoog en laag nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Unpitched percussion instrument': instruments producing sounds of indeterminate pitch, listing 'All rattles, for example maracas'; scrapers such as the güiro are conventionally unpitched. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unpitched_percussion_instrument . 'Geen vaste plek' correctly says 'no definite pitch'; it does not say they cannot sound brighter or duller than one another.

items.bewering: Elkeen van die timbila het hoë en lae klanke binne een instrument.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Timbila': the mbila has up to nineteen keys, the dibinda ten, and even the gulu three or four, so every size carries several pitches; MFA Boston mbila record: keys with graded gourd resonators. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbila ; https://www.mfa.org/collections/object/xylophone-mbila-and-one-mallet-50750

items.bewering: 'n Groep tromme wat ewe styf gespan is, loop van klein na groot en van hoog na laag.
items.bron: Rochester PHY103 'Drums' membrane formula (at equal tension and skin, frequency falls as diameter rises); Wikipedia 'Unpitched percussion instrument': smaller tom-toms, bongos and timbales are tuned higher than larger ones.

items.bewering: Luister na 'n musiekstuk uit Afrika. Let op watter instrumente of stemme hoog klink, watter laag, watter die maat hou en watter bo-oor die res speel.
items.bron: The block is a listening instruction. The only thing it assumes, that in African ensembles some parts keep the beat while others play over them, is supported: in Venda domba music the thungwa sets the basic beat while the ngoma and murumba play their own rhythms (ERA, Venda Girls, https://era.anthropology.ac.uk/Era_Resources/Era/VendaGirls/Links/Mu_I_Fig01.html).

items.bewering: Kwartaal 3 se drama het uit 'n stimulus gegroei. Julle het karakters gebou, liedjies gekies en 'n klankbaan gemaak. Kyk na 'n speler se postuur, gebare en gesigsuitdrukking.
items.blok: Praat oor julle eie en mekaar se optredes
items.bron: CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6, Gr 4 Kwartaal 3 (printed p. 35): Topic 2 'Characters, using props as stimulus ... Consider body language, posture and gesture'; Topic 3 'Building a drama from a stimulus: characters ...', 'Relate character of the chosen songs to suit characters in the drama', 'Sound pictures using instruments ... to create a soundtrack for the drama'. DBE multi-grade ATP for Creative Arts, Term 3 Gr 4, says the same. Note for a person, not a fact error: CAPS says the order of topics within the term is not fixed, so the past tense assumes the school taught Topics 2 and 3 before Topic 4.

items.bewering: 'n Trom en 'n marimba klink anders, al klink albei ewe hoog en ewe hard. Daardie verskil noem ons toonkleur.
items.blok: Praat oor julle eie en mekaar se optredes
items.bron: Acoustical Society of America (ANSI) definition of timbre: the attribute by which a listener judges two sounds with the same loudness and pitch to be dissimilar; also called tone colour. Wikipedia 'Timbre', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbre

items.bewering: toonhoogte: Hoe hoog of hoe laag 'n klank is.
items.bron: Standard definition of pitch as the perceived highness or lowness of a sound (schoolphysics.co.uk, as above). True when read on its own.

items.bewering: volume: Hoe hard of hoe sag 'n klank is.
items.bron: Loudness/volume as the loud-soft attribute, set by how hard a sound source is made to vibrate (classroom sound activities above; ASA definitions of loudness). True when read on its own.

items.bewering: toonkleur: Wat twee instrumente anders laat klink, al klink hulle ewe hoog en hard.
items.bron: ASA timbre definition (as above). True when read on its own; it applies to voices too, but the entry does not deny that.

items.bewering: vibreer: Om baie vinnig heen en weer te beweeg.
items.bron: Collins via Dictionary.com 'vibrate': 'to move or cause to move back and forth rapidly'; Vocabulary.com: 'extremely rapid back-and-forth movement'. https://www.dictionary.com/browse/vibrate

items.bewering: slaginstrument: 'n Instrument wat klank maak as jy dit slaan, skud of skraap.
items.bron: Arapahoe Philharmonic 'Instruments of the Orchestra': percussion sound 'is made by striking, scraping or shaking' (https://www.arapahoe-phil.org/instruments-of-the-orchestra); Wikipedia 'Percussion instrument'. True when read on its own.

items.bewering: familie: 'n Groep instrumente wat saamgegroepeer word volgens die manier waarop hulle klank maak.
items.bron: Arapahoe Philharmonic and LibreTexts 'Instruments' (Prince George's CC): orchestral families (strings, woodwind, brass, percussion) are sorted by how each instrument produces its sound. True when read on its own and consistent with the block's 'groep binne die familie'.

items.bewering: xilofoon: 'n Instrument met houtlatte wat jy met stokkies slaan.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Xylophone': wooden bars struck by mallets; Collins: 'wooden bars of graduated length'. Metal-barred instruments are glockenspiels, so 'houtlatte' is the right boundary. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xylophone

items.bewering: timbila: Die Chopi se xilofone, met 'n hol dop onder elke houtlat.
items.bron: UNESCO ICH 'Chopi Timbila': 'Under each wooden slat, a resonator made out of calabashes is fastened' (https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/chopi-timbila-00133); Wikipedia 'Timbila': gourds or masala-fruit shells as resonators. Sources differ on the material (calabash, masala shell, wild citrus shell), but every one is a hollow shell under each key, which is all the entry says.

items.bewering: ngoma: Die grootste en diepste trom wat die VhaVenda gebruik, met beesvel oor uitgeholde hout.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English 'ngoma': 'A large, single-headed drum of the Venda people' (https://dsae.co.za/entry/ngoma/e05157); ERA 'Venda Music' (after Kirby 1934): ngoma is the large drum and the bass of the ngoma-thungwa-murumba set, body carved out of solid wood (https://era.anthropology.ac.uk/Era_Resources/Era/VendaGirls/VendaMusic/Mu_I_Text2.html); museum record: ox-hide head (https://wmic.net/venda-ngoma-drum/). 'Grootste' and 'diepste' both hold. Read on its own the entry is still true; the DSAE notes that the same word means drum (and dance) more generally in East Africa, which the entry does not deny.

items.bewering: hosho: 'n Kalbasratel van Zimbabwe met sade binne, in pare geskud.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Hosho (instrument)': Zimbabwean gourd rattles filled with hota seeds, usually played in pairs, one in each hand (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hosho_(instrument)); Grinnell College collection, Bira instruments.

items.bewering: karakter: Die mens, dier, ding of opgemaakte wese wat 'n speler in 'n drama voorstel.
items.bron: University of the Free State drama glossary: a character is 'a fictional or representational person, figure, or persona' that an actor interprets and embodies (https://pokello.ufs.ac.za/s/PUO/item/29654); person or animal also in literary definitions. 'Ding' is right for a personified object played by an actor, which is common in children's drama. True when read on its own.

items.bewering: postuur: Hoe iemand sy lyf hou terwyl hy sit, staan of beweeg.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's: 'the position in which you hold your body when standing or sitting'; WordNet: 'characteristic way of bearing one's body'; Wiktionary: 'the way a person holds and positions their body' (https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/posture). 'Of beweeg' goes a little beyond the sit/stand wording but matches the general sense and CAPS's use of character posture in movement work.

items.bewering: gebare: Bewegings van die lyf, soos die hande, kop of arms, wat iets sê.
items.bron: Standard dictionary sense of gesture: 'a movement of a part of the body, especially a hand or the head, to express an idea or meaning' (Oxford wording, reproduced in the body-language sources found); gestures are also made with shoulders and arms.

items.bewering: gesigsuitdrukking: Die manier waarop jou gesig wys hoe jy voel.
items.bron: Auslan Signbank: facial expression is 'the way your face shows what you are thinking or feeling' (https://auslan.org.au/dictionary/words/facial%20expression-1.html); Vocabulary.com.

items.bewering: emosie: 'n Gevoel wat vanself in jou opkom en weer wegraak.
items.bron: Paul Ekman Group 'Universal emotions': 'we don't choose to feel them, they just happen to us automatically'; 'emotions typically don't last longer than an hour' (https://www.paulekman.com/universal-emotions/); APA handbook (Dess 2010): 'a relatively brief episode'. 'Vanself' means unchosen, not uncaused; Ekman adds that emotions arise in response to a stimulus, and the entry does not deny that.

items.bewering: rekwisiete: Die voorwerpe wat spelers in 'n drama gebruik, soos 'n hoed of 'n stok.
items.bron: CAPS Life Skills Gr 4 Kwartaal 3 resources: 'Props such as cans, suitcases, hats, newspapers, balls ...' (printed p. 35). In professional theatre a worn hat sits on the costume/prop border, but Eric Hart's 'Categories of Props' places hats among costume props, a kind of prop (https://www.props.eric-hart.com/features/categories-of-props/).

items.bewering: ruggraat: Die ry klein beentjies wat in die middel van jou rug loop.
items.bron: Britannica 'vertebral column': a series of vertebrae (33 counting the fused sacral and coccygeal ones) running from the skull to the pelvis along the back (https://www.britannica.com/science/vertebral-column). 'Klein' is relative; acceptable at Grade 4.

items.bewering: isolasie: Om een deel van die lyf alleen te beweeg terwyl die res stil bly.
items.bron: Dance usage: isolation means moving one body part while the rest of the body stays still or controlled (Rockstar Academy 'Isolation dance', https://www.rockstaracademy.com/blog/isolation-dance ; Grade 3 arts curriculum resource). CAPS Gr 4 T3 uses it in exactly this sense ('Body part isolations').

items.bewering: do-so: Vyf note wat na mekaar al hoër klink: do, re, mi, fa en so.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4 Kwartaal 3: 'Recognise melodies in range of 5th using tonic solfa (doh to soh)'; doh-re-mi-fa-soh are the first five rising degrees of the major scale in tonic sol-fa.

items.bewering: klankprent: 'n Prentjie of storie wat julle net met klanke vertel.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4 Kwartaal 3 key term 'sound picture (soundscape)' and 'Sound pictures using instruments ... to create a soundtrack for the drama'; Drama Resource 'Soundscapes': a group builds 'a sound picture of a theme' using voices and body percussion (https://dramaresource.com/soundscapes/).

opsomming: All 44 checkable claims hold up against sources, including both superlatives (the ngoma as the largest and deepest Venda drum, the chilanzane highest and the gulu lowest of the timbila) and the ruler comparison, whose mapping holds; the only thing worth a person's glance is not a fact error but the drama block's past tense, which assumes the term's drama was taught before this lesson although CAPS leaves the order of topics within a term open.
